newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs rally into close, bellies hold losses.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs rally into close, bellies hold losses.

text.p: CME hog futures rallied into the close to end higher while pork bellies remained under pressure in current year contracts.

Hog futures closed 0.925 cent per lb higher to unchanged with July up 0.675 at 80.025 cents. June expired earlier at 80.725, off 0.250 on the day. Pork bellies ended 2.000 lower to 1.025 higher with July off most at 76.900 cents.

Hog futures rallied after running into long term technical support early. Short covering also developed on an oversold condition and expectations that cash markets would firm later next week, traders said.

Spillover pressure from USDA's cut Thursday in its forecast for U.S. pork exports gave way to long-term technical support. Hog futures sank to a level from which they have rallied before and sellers were reluctant to pressure the market further, sources noted.
USDA on Thursday lowered its 1997 estimate for pork exports by 105 million lbs to 1.250 billion lbs and lowered 1998 projections by 115 million lbs to 1.465 billion lbs.
R.J. O'Brien notably bought July early and Rand Financials bought after being a net seller early, pit sources said.
In hog options, Iowa Grain continued to do risk reversals buying October 74 calls and selling 68 puts and buying piece 72 calls and selling 64 puts, pit sources added.

Pork belly futures staged a rally before midsession after tumbling the daily limit in July early but turned weak again on bearish fundamentals. Futures recovered when early fund liquidation subsided and talk circulated that packers may cut slaughter rates next week. However, this failed to offset pressure from the recent slide in cash belly prices and a bearish chart picture when futures recently declined to two- month lows, traders said.
Domestic and export demand for bellies remains slack despite the recent drop in values, they said.
ADM Investor Services, Refco, FIMAT Futures USA and ABN Chicogo Corp were notable sellers on the early price break. Scattered commercial buying was cited at times, pit sources said.
